question: Does the authored-at timezone detector separate a maintainer-identity ATO from the maintainer's own commits -- and does the signal survive a multi-commit burst?

provenance.notes: Sixth Shai-Hulud wave, disclosed as ChainDrop. Push credential belonged to maintainer jaredwray; initial access unconfirmed. Payload is a `preinstall` hook plus committed .claude/settings.json and .vscode/tasks.json agent auto-run configs that cross-reference each other, so opening a checkout in an IDE or agent session executes it with no install.
provenance.recovered: Objects were deleted from the default branch. Recovered 2026-08-08 by fetch-by-SHA; GitHub still serves them by full SHA. Mirrored to upstream-mirrors/keyv.git under refs/mirror/<sha>. Do not rely on upstream remaining willing to serve them.
provenance.corrects_public_reporting: Public writeups state the keyv commits were authored as spoofed github-actions[bot]/claude. That holds for d8c850c7 only. The three payload commits carry the real maintainer identity Jared Wray <me@jaredwray.com>, unsigned, so keyv is a genuine known-author ATO rather than a spoofed-author case. Reporting also called the timezone undeterminable; the objects carry it.

habitual_offset.note: Measured over jaredwray's full 2,231-commit authored history in the mirror, before the incident.
habitual_offset.claim: Exactly three +0000 commits exist in the entire history, and they are exactly the three payload commits.

malicious_3.subject: keyv: add setup.mjs and Math_Symbol.js to all @keyv/* packages

benign_human_control.subject: etcd - fix: Use Keyv default serializer for value envelope (#2041)

roles.malicious_1: First payload commit. Maximum signal: this offset has never been seen for this identity.
roles.malicious_2: Second payload commit. first_seen has already flipped False -- poisoned by malicious_1.
roles.malicious_3: Third payload commit. Mode support decayed 20 -> 18.
roles.bot_config_commit: Agent-config commit, genuinely authored by github-actions[bot]. No baseline exists for that identity, so the detector must report an unknown mode rather than an anomaly.
roles.benign_human_control: Last clean jaredwray commit before the attack, 2h15m earlier. Matched in-repo negative.
roles.benign_bot_control: Legitimate release-automation commit at +0000. The load-bearing false-positive control: same offset as the attack, but no drift, because the bot identity's own baseline is +0000.

burst_decay.note: Per-commit evaluation of a burst is NOT independent -- the detector's own history window ingests the attacker's earlier commits.

window_sweep.note: prior_count and mode measured at max_author_history_commits in (5,10,20,50); the drift signal is window-insensitive here, but prior_count decay is not.

inversion_threshold.note: Latent hazard, NOT realized by this incident. The mode flips to the attacker's offset once malicious commits exceed half the window, at which point drift collapses to 0 and the detector inverts. With the default window of 20 that needs 11 payload commits; keyv had 3. Pinned so that shrinking the window or meeting a longer burst fails loudly.

why_this_fixture: First real ground truth for the authored-at timezone detector: two identities, five years of habitual offsets, and an attack that is separated perfectly.

The +0000 offset is not itself the signal -- legitimate release automation in this same repo commits at +0000. The signal is drift against a per-identity baseline, and the benign_bot_control pins that distinction.
Documents that burst position changes the score, which any per-commit evaluation harness must account for or it will understate the detector and hide the inversion.
